symptom: gitignore hid the deployed free catalogue
root_cause: The ignore patterns were written as "apps/" and "paid/" with no leading slash, and git matches an unanchored pattern at every depth. site/apps/ is the deployed free catalogue, so the Friday job's "git add -A" silently skipped the entire directory.
evidence: git check-ignore site/apps/probe/app/index.html returned 0 (ignored). Run 38311010124 committed data/candidate.json and no app.
verification: selftest_audit passes; the guard was confirmed by reverting .gitignore and watching it report the problem.

symptom: committed state carried the build machine's absolute paths
root_cause: stage_app stored paid_dir and installer with str(path.resolve()), while the candidate field beside them was correctly relative. data/candidate.json is committed, so the Friday runner's own folder layout was published to every other machine, where it resolves to nothing.
fix: Both stored relative to the repo via _rel(), which reports a path outside the repo as empty rather than absolute.
regression_test: selftest_audit.py checks no tracked state file holds a Windows absolute path.
verification: selftest_audit reports 0 problems and the committed file now reads paid/dev-converter.

symptom: NSIS installed but makensis was not on PATH
root_cause: choco install nsis succeeds and writes the machine PATH, but a GitHub Actions step runs with the PATH it started with, so the install is invisible to the step that asked for it.
evidence: Run 38385940018: "The term 'makensis' is not recognized" on the line immediately after "The install of nsis was successful".
fix: Both jobs resolve makensis.exe from its install location, print where it was found, fail with a real message if absent, and add the directory to GITHUB_PATH.
regression_test: verified by the next run reaching the installer step
verification: Run 38401429866 generated and committed; the generate job completed with makensis resolved.

symptom: rate limit backoff spent the whole retry budget inside one window
root_cause: A 429 slept 10s then 20s, but the allowance is per minute, so every attempt landed inside the same window and received the same refusal. The verifier then reported the app as unrepairable.
evidence: Run 38401720935: rounds 2 to 4 each failed with 429 on openai/gpt-oss-120b and ended "4 controls still dead".
fix: _rate_limit_wait() waits out the meter's own window plus a margin, still growing so an exhausted key does not spin.
regression_test: stubbed sender: a 429 on the first two attempts returns the third successfully, after 65s then 90s
verification: verified locally with a stubbed provider

symptom: exposure gates refused the app the pipeline had just staged
root_cause: The generate job commits the free edition an hour before the verifier writes its catalog entry, so in between the app is in site/apps/ and in no catalog. Both gates read that as a leak and failed the run before the verifier could ever run.
evidence: Run 38400432942: "site/apps/dev-converter-basic is not a known free edition and must not be public".
repro: python check_repo_hygiene.py against the freshly generated app
fix: Both now read data/candidate.json and accept the app it names. Anything else, including a leftover from a retired product, is still reported.
regression_test: check_repo_hygiene.py and check_exposure.py both pass with the staged app present

symptom: a generated app could not parse, so every control looked dead
root_cause: Three separate faults. make_app undid the model's JSON escaping one level at a time, so a doubly escaped reply kept its backslashes. Decoding only the quotes still left template literal markers escaped, which closes the template early. Independently, the model mistyped one closing delimiter. In each case the script block failed to parse, so no handler ran, so every control was reported dead, so the repair loop spent its budget patching controls that were never broken.
evidence: app_scanner on dev-converter: pageerror "Invalid or unexpected token", 6 of 6 controls dead.
fix: _unescape() decodes the escapes a JSON string uses and repeats until stable; js_syntax_errors() checks every script block, using node when the runner has it and escaping plus delimiter checks when it does not; html_looks_fine() refuses to stage an app that cannot parse.
regression_test: jscheck_selftest.py proves the fallback does not cry wolf on ten valid snippets; audit_selftest.py checks the real generated app parses
verification: the next generate run reported "attempt 1 ok" and the app scans with 0 dead and 0 errors

symptom: the scanner refused working apps, so nothing could ever publish
root_cause: The probe demanded that clicking any control change the DOM, storage or an input value. Three classes of control cannot do that and are not broken: a select the app reads, a submit button in a form with required fields, and a button that opens a file picker.
evidence: dev-converter: dead=[4 controls] on an app that converts correctly.
repro: python app_scanner.py against the generated app
fix: An id the app's script reads is an input, not a button. Submit buttons get empty required fields filled first. The file inputs' click is intercepted, and a click that reached one is reported skipped.
regression_test: scanner_selftest.py builds a page with four genuinely broken controls, all of which must still be reported dead
verification: scanner_selftest.py: FAILURES: none. dev-converter: dead=[], skipped=['BUTTON:Import My Data']

symptom: the javascript check crashed on a Windows pipe
root_cause: The node branch passed the script as text, so the pipe encoded it with the runner's default codepage. An arrow character in the generated app raised UnicodeEncodeError in subprocess._stdin_write and the whole generate job died before the check could report anything.
evidence: Run 38400432942: UnicodeEncodeError, charmap codec cannot encode U+2192, in subprocess._stdin_write.
fix: The check encodes to UTF-8 itself and decodes the diagnostics the same way, so the codepage of whatever machine is running cannot change the verdict.
regression_test: nodecheck_selftest.py runs the node branch against a stub and fails if the arrow raises

symptom: the paid publish outcome was recorded and then thrown away
root_cause: The step that records the itch.io outcome has no id, so the PUBLISHED value it writes to GITHUB_OUTPUT belongs to that step and is read by nothing. The job reports success whether or not the paid edition was actually published, which is the reporting defect the audit is required to eliminate.
evidence: Workflow inspection: the only step referencing steps.publish is the one that writes the unused output.
fix: The record step now has id: paid, writes the outcome to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, and a final gate reads it. The gate runs after the free edition has been deployed, so one dead destination does not cost the customer the release that worked, but the job fails with a plain message. ALLOW_FREE_ONLY accepts the partial release deliberately.
regression_test: parsed friday-verify.yml; steps.paid exists and the gate is the final step
verification: Run 38416539839 executed the gate and reported the paid edition was not published, instead of reporting success. That is the first evidence the gate runs.

symptom: a debug backup file is committed to the published site
root_cause: qa_loop writes index.rN.bak beside the app it is repairing and nothing removes it. git add -A committed one into site/, which GitHub Pages serves. Development-only material shipped in a release.
fix: qa_loop writes per-round backups to data/qa_backups/ instead of beside the app, and check_exposure refuses to pass if any .bak, .trial.html, .py or .tmp reaches site/.
regression_test: planted index.r4.bak in the published tree; check_exposure reported it
verification: check_exposure ok after removal; index.r3.bak untracked and deleted

symptom: committed per-minute token counter was read as another runner's usage
root_cause: The Friday job's blanket git add committed data/token_usage.json. It is live rate-limit state for whichever machine is running, so each later run on another runner began its allowance from a total it did not earn.
fix: The file and its temporary siblings are ignored.
regression_test: cleanroom_selftest.py copies what git tracks and asserts it survives

symptom: an unreadable counter read as zero, so the pipeline kept spending
root_cause: _load() swallowed a parse error and returned {}, which spent() read as zero tokens used. affordable() then answered yes on every call. In a counter, zero is the answer that allows spending.
evidence: Executed the pre-fix module from 0274226 against a corrupt state file: spent=0, affordable(8000,100)=True.
fix: An unreadable or non-dict state is reported on stderr and read as unknown; spent() returns a figure above any limit. The write is atomic.
regression_test: audit_selftest.py writes truncated, list and numeric states and checks each is unknown, not zero, and leaves nothing affordable

symptom: an unreadable budget read as zero hours, so jobs were approved
root_cause: The same fail-open shape. A corrupt budget.json returned an empty budget, which read as a month with nothing spent, so check() approved work on a month that may already have spent all thirty hours. The module docstring claimed the hours were committed and could not quietly reset, which was false: 380e29e had deliberately untracked the file.
evidence: Executed the pre-fix module from 0274226: check() returned 0 (approved) with a corrupt state.
fix: check() refuses outright when the hours cannot be read; the write is atomic; the docstring describes what is actually true.
regression_test: audit_selftest.py checks a readable budget approves and corrupt ones refuse

symptom: a release could die on a traceback and still have claimed to save
root_cause: save() logged its success line before writing, and neither it nor publish_public() caught the write error, so an unattended job exited on a traceback and main() returned 0 either way.
evidence: Executed the pre-fix module against a read-only state file and against a read-only public file: PermissionError traceback, exit 1.
repro: exec of git show 0274226:update_state.py in a copied tree
fix: Both report whether they wrote, neither claims a save it cannot prove, and main() exits non-zero when either failed.
regression_test: audit_selftest.py makes the state file read-only and checks no traceback, a non-zero exit and no claimed save

symptom: the site advertised a paid product that was not for sale
root_cause: set_itch_url.valid() required at least one path segment, computed as len(path.strip('/').split('/')) >= 1. An account front page has the path '/', so strip gives the empty string, and ''.split('/') is [''], which has length one and passed. The catalog therefore held the account page as the product URL, publish_paid.py saw a URL present and a price in range, and set published=True.
evidence: The live store was fetched during the audit and lists zero products. site/apps.json carried published=true with itch_url pointing at the account page, and e2e_product.py reported the catalog as published while the itch.io check failed.
repro: python publish_paid.py password-manager, which exited 0 and left the tier marked published
fix: valid() now requires a non-empty first path segment and an account subdomain. publish_paid.py refuses on the same ground and then fetches the page, refusing to mark anything on sale unless the response contains a purchase or download section. The catalog was corrected: the paid tier is published=false with an empty itch_url until a real product page exists.
verification: itchurl_selftest.py: FAILURES: none. publish_paid.py password-manager now exits 1 with a plain message. check_exposure ok.
uncertainty: The upload to itch.io has still never been executed, because the credentials exist only as repository secrets. That the store is empty is confirmed by fetching the live page.

symptom: the installer job built the wrong product because a slug went stale
root_cause: build_paid_only took the slug from data/published.json, which the verify job writes and which was committed. Two dispatches in quick succession left published.json naming dev-converter while the artifact uploaded in that run held unit-converter, so the installer job looked for a directory that had never been uploaded.
evidence: Run 38416539839 failed with "no paid build at paid/dev-converter". Downloading the paid-build artifact from that same run shows unit-converter/app/index.html and nothing named dev-converter, so the correct build was present and was simply not the one it looked for.
repro: gh run download 38416539839 -n paid-build, then compare what arrived with what data/published.json named
fix: When the recorded slug has no build, exactly one uploaded build is used and the mismatch is logged and recorded as RETRIED. Two or more is ambiguous and is refused rather than guessed. data/published.json is untracked, because the artifact is the authority on what was actually built and carrying the slug through git only risks it being one release stale.
verification: paidbuild_selftest.py: FAILURES: none, covering the named build, the stale-slug fallback, the ambiguous refusal, and no builds at all.
uncertainty: The itch.io upload is still unexecuted; the credentials exist only as repository secrets.
